text:
ConocoPhillips fell 1.1% today to $134.26, reversing most of the gains it posted over the prior three trading days. The decline came despite a supportive backdrop for oil refiners: diesel prices hit record highs due to refinery outages in Russia and Ukraine, while crude oil itself held firm around $91–96 per barrel depending on location. This kind of move—pullback even as underlying fuel costs spike—often reflects profit-taking after a sharp three-day rally rather than deteriorating fundamentals.

The broader geopolitical picture remains volatile but ultimately supportive for refiners. Sanctions on Iran and Russia are constraining global refinery capacity, and the EU's formal entry into U.S.-led sanctions adds structural pressure on fuel supply. However, the stock's near-flat performance over two weeks suggests investors are weighing the refinery tailwind against uncertainty over how long these supply disruptions will persist and whether crude prices themselves can sustain gains if economic growth slows.
